Occurrence of Invertebrate Fauna in 
Schirmacher Oasis, Antarctica 
MOHOMMAD ARIF 
Defence Agricultural Research Laboratory 
Panda,pithoragarh-262.501 
     Abstract 
The Schirmacher Oasis region in East Antarctica was surveyed during the eleventh 
Indian expedition to Antarctica in the austral summer of 1991-92. Samples of water, soil, 
moss, lichen and algae showed presence of invertebrate fauna like earthworm, nematods, 
mites, springtail, dipterous flies, larvae and a single specimen of moth. 
Introduction 
Terrestrial animals of Antarctica arc confined to microbes and a few small 
invertebrates. A total of 387 invertebrate fauna have so far been recorded in the 
sub-Antarctic, 127 in maritime Antarctica and 107 on the continent itself; many 
of these occurring in more than one of these zones (May,1988 and Laws,I989). 
These are mostly microscopic, which live in the plantlitter, moss, peat, soil, 
lichen, algae, birds' litter md in the micro-climate under the rocks. They range 
from protozoa, rotifers, tradigrades and nematodes to arthropods. Out of 137 
species of Arthropods reported from Antarctica, the principal Arthropod groups 
represent Acarina (70 species of mites), Mallophaga (37 species of biting lice), 
Collembola (20 species of springtaila), Anoplura (5 species of sucking lice), 
Diptera (2 species of midges), Siphonoptera (1 species of fleas) and Coleoptera 
(2 species of beetles probably alien or known from islands near the Antarctic 
Peninsula). 
Ingole et al.( 1987) have reported 14.57 % nematode 0.54 % acarina, 22.31 % 
protozoa, 0.60 % oligochaeta and 38.6 % resting stages of micro-invertebrates 
from the aquatic micro fauna of Priyadarshini Lake of Schirmacher Oasis. 
Ingole and Parulekar (1987) reported Teratacephalus sp. of nematode from 
water-moss communities at the same location. So far unidentified mite and 
springtail have also been reported from Schirmacher Oasis (Richter et al., 1989).
